rows.reason: Output-stationary dataflow is a decided architectural choice made at the origin; not a performance figure with spread.
INT8 x INT8 -> INT32 with requantization is a decided number format and rounding rule; there is no distribution to characterise.
The supported operation set is a decided feature list; presence of an operation is not statistical.
Wishbone B4 classic, 32-bit, slave is a decided protocol choice, checked by protocol-level testbenches rather than statistics.
ARRAY_N is a single decided RTL parameter (legal values {4, 8, 16}, stamped RTL implements 4 and 8); a chosen design size, not a measured quantity.
The integer golden model is an exact reference; results are compared bit for bit, so there is no tolerance or spread.
Testbenches are bit-exact against the golden model; any mismatch is a failure, with no yield or statistical spread.
8 x 8 (ARRAY_N = 8) is a ratified design size (decision 0005), not a sampled quantity.

Memory is represented by abstract macro views generated from a parameter table; the representation, banking and geometry are design choices, and the Liberty numbers are labelled placeholders, not a distribution.

The predicted clock is a post-route STA figure bounded per corner by static timing analysis, which is deterministic for a given netlist, parasitics and Liberty views; it is not a Monte Carlo or distributional result.
SS (0.63 V / 100 C) is a static corner evaluated by deterministic STA against fixed Liberty files, not a sampled distribution.
TT (0.7 V / 25 C) is a static corner evaluated by deterministic STA against fixed Liberty files, not a sampled distribution.

FF (0.77 V / 0 C) is a provisional static corner evaluated by deterministic STA against fixed Liberty files; the SIMPLE-group header anomaly is disclosed in the spec and is a data question, not a statistical one.
Quoting spec/npu.md: "This is a digital block closed on static corners; there is no statistical row." Closure is by static STA at the ratified PVT corners.
The DRC deck hash, klt pin and LVS options are fixed, pinned inputs to deterministic rule checks.
Flat and hierarchical DRC/LVS runs are deterministic rule checks that either report zero violations or do not; runtime is recorded separately as a tool-scaling record.
Abstract macros are black boxes in DRC and LVS; this is a recorded deterministic-check limitation, not a statistical measure.
LVS is a deterministic netlist comparison: the extracted netlist matches the reference with no mismatches, or it does not.
Waivers are committed, human-approved entries against deterministic DRC rule ids; the waiver count is an exact integer, not a statistic.
Runtime and peak memory of deterministic DRC and LVS runs are recorded as evidence per array size; they are run records, not a sampled analog or statistical quantity.
